guides.definition: A standards-mode HTML document starts with a doctype and an html element. Metadata belongs in head, while rendered page content belongs in body.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: The page's primary BCP 47 language tag.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Text shown in the browser tab and used by assistive technology.

parameters.name: heading
parameters.description: The visible primary heading.

examples.title: Start a standards-mode page
examples.code: Hello, web
examples.explanation: The metadata establishes encoding and responsive sizing before the main landmark contains the visible page heading.

guides.definition: Semantic sectioning and grouping elements communicate the purpose of page regions to browsers, assistive technology, and maintainers.

parameters.name: siteName
parameters.description: The product or site heading.

parameters.name: navigation
parameters.description: Links placed in the primary navigation region.

parameters.name: heading
parameters.description: The heading for the primary content.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A paragraph of primary content.

parameters.name: footer
parameters.description: Supporting footer content.

examples.title: Describe the page structure
examples.code:
Hypershell

Workspace

Build something useful.

examples.explanation: Each region has a native role, while the navigation label distinguishes it from any other nav regions.

guides.definition: An a element with an href attribute creates a hyperlink. Link text should describe the destination without relying on surrounding prose.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A relative or absolute URL.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Meaningful text describing the destination.

examples.title: Link to documentation
examples.explanation: The href identifies the destination and the visible text explains what the user will open.

guides.definition: The img alt attribute provides a text alternative when the image carries meaning. figure and figcaption associate supporting caption content with it.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The image URL or relative file path.

parameters.name: alternative
parameters.description: A concise replacement for the image's meaning.
parameters.defaultValue: Hypershell workspace with editor and browser tabs

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The intrinsic image width in CSS pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The intrinsic image height in CSS pixels.

parameters.name: caption
parameters.description: Visible supporting text associated with the image.

examples.title: Caption a product screenshot
examples.explanation: Explicit dimensions reserve layout space, alt text replaces the image's meaning, and the caption remains visible to everyone.

guides.definition: A label associated through for and id gives a form control an accessible name. Native input types and required constraints provide useful browser behavior.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The URL that receives submitted form data.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: The form submission method, normally get or post.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A document-unique identifier shared with the label.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Text naming the input.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The key used in submitted form data.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: A native input type appropriate for the expected data.

parameters.name: button
parameters.description: Text describing the submission action.

examples.title: Collect an email address
examples.code:
<form action="/subscribe" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email address</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Subscribe</button>
</form>
examples.explanation: The explicit label names the input, type=email enables email-specific validation, and required prevents an empty native submission.

guides.definition: Use ul when order is not meaningful and ol when sequence or ranking matters. Each direct item is represented by li.

parameters.name: listType
parameters.description: Use ul for unordered content or ol for an ordered sequence.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: The first list item.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: The second list item.

parameters.name: third
parameters.description: The third list item.

examples.title: List development stages
examples.explanation: An ordered list communicates that the stages have a meaningful sequence.

guides.definition: table is for genuinely tabular data. caption names the table and th scope attributes identify whether headings apply to columns or rows.

parameters.name: caption
parameters.description: A concise name for the data set.

parameters.name: firstHeading
parameters.description: The first column heading.

parameters.name: secondHeading
parameters.description: The second column heading.

parameters.name: firstValue
parameters.description: The first row's first value.

parameters.name: secondValue
parameters.description: The first row's second value.

examples.title: Show a build status
examples.explanation: The caption names the table and column scopes let tools associate both data cells with their headings.

guides.definition: details provides a native disclosure widget and summary supplies its always-visible label. The open attribute controls its initial state.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: The clickable label for the disclosure.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The content revealed when the widget opens.
parameters.defaultValue: It loads the saved page in a Hypershell browser tab.

examples.title: Explain browser preview
examples.code:
What does Preview do?

It loads the saved page in a Hypershell browser tab.
examples.explanation: The browser supplies keyboard, pointer, and open-state behavior for the disclosure.

guides.definition: A link element with rel=stylesheet creates an external resource link whose CSS rules apply to the document when loaded.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A URL or path relative to the HTML document.

examples.title: Load the project stylesheet
examples.explanation: A relative path resolves beside the saved HTML file, so local browser preview can load styles.css from the same folder.

guides.definition: A script element with type=module loads JavaScript as a module, enabling import and export syntax and executing after document parsing.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A URL or path to browser-compatible JavaScript.

examples.title: Load the browser entry module
examples.explanation: The browser parses app.js as a module. TypeScript source must first be compiled to browser-compatible JavaScript.
